sections.markdown:
## C — Sharing the road: keeping space and staying out of blind spots, pedestrians and sidewalks, yielding to and moving over for emergency vehicles, stopping for school buses, motorcycles, passing bicyclists, and truck no-zones
Knowledge domain: how to share Wisconsin roads safely with pedestrians, emergency vehicles, school buses, motorcycles, bicycles and large trucks, including the stopping and spacing distances the knowledge test asks about.

FACT_ID: sec11-F01 | anchor: A01
The more distance you keep between yourself and other road users, the more time you have to react. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F02 | anchor: A01
On multi-lane roads, avoid riding right beside another driver; move ahead of the vehicle or drop back. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F03 | anchor: A01
Give parked vehicles along the road extra room, and avoid lingering where another driver's view of you is blocked. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F04 | anchor: A01
Stay alert for children and others who may run into the road without looking, and give extra room to pedestrians, confused drivers and anyone who cannot see you. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F05 | anchor: A01
Driving on a sidewalk is illegal except to cross it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F06 | anchor: A01
When you see emergency lights and hear sirens, move to the roadside and stay stopped there until the emergency vehicle has gone by. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F07 | anchor: A01
Never stop in the middle of an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F08 | anchor: A01
When approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, move into a lane that is not next to it and stay in the farthest lane until you have passed it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F09 | anchor: A01
When a police car is stopped on the roadside with lights and siren on, the law requires you to move over or slow down to give the officers room. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F10 | anchor: A01
When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, stop at least 20 feet away from it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F11 | anchor: A01
You must stop for a school bus with flashing red lights whether it is on your side of the road or the opposite side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F12 | anchor: A01
Watch for children around a stopped school bus, and go only after its red lights stop flashing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F13 | anchor: A01
On a divided highway, where a barrier separates the opposing lanes, you need not stop for a school bus on the other side. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F14 | anchor: A01
Motorcycles are lightweight and can stop faster than most vehicles, so give them extra room, especially when following one. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F15 | anchor: A01
Around motorcycles, be extra aware and check your blind spots before moving, and wait until it is safe to pass. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0055]

FACT_ID: sec11-F16 | anchor: A02
A bicyclist may use the whole traffic lane, and you should not share a lane with one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F17 | anchor: A02
Bicyclists can move into your path quickly and without warning, so wait for oncoming traffic to clear before you pass one. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F18 | anchor: A02
Leave at least three feet between your vehicle and a bicyclist when passing. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F19 | anchor: A02
Bicycles should carry reflectors or lights, but some do not, so stay watchful around them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F20 | anchor: A02
No-zones are the areas around large vehicles where the driver cannot see you, reaching about 200 feet behind and 20 feet in front of a large truck. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F21 | anchor: A02
Big trucks cannot see cars that are close behind them or right in front of them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

FACT_ID: sec11-F22 | anchor: A02
If you are in a truck's no-zone, either speed up or drop back so the driver can see you, and when passing, get through the blind spot quickly. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0056]

Misconceptions: a stopped school bus on the far side of an undivided road still requires you to stop; only a divided highway with a barrier removes that duty; you do not stop inside an intersection for an emergency vehicle; a bicyclist may use the whole lane, so you do not squeeze past inside the same lane; a truck driver cannot see a car tucked close behind the trailer even though the car can see the truck; a motorcycle ahead can stop quicker than you, so following closely is risky.
Mnemonics: lights and sirens mean pull right and stop; move over or slow down for a stopped squad car; red lights on the bus mean stop well back and wait for the flashing to end; three feet for a bike; near a big truck, speed up or drop back.
Glossary: blind spot means an area where another driver cannot see you; no-zone means the large blind area around a big truck; divided highway means a road with a barrier between opposite directions; emergency vehicle means a vehicle responding with emergency lights and sirens; pedestrian means a person on foot.
